title: Paint Anything: Toward Any-Color Controllable Image Generation and Editing
claim: One prompt interface using explicit values gives precise control over attributes in both editing and generation, shown through diverse samples.
layout: 2 rows: 6-image recolor strip above, 3 generated images, captions underneath
description: A gallery figure in two rows. The top row has six images of the same paper lantern lamp. The first is a gray original captioned 'set the lamp's color to'. The other five show it recolored to cyan, green, pale yellow, purple and pink. Each has a caption bar filled with its hex code, such as #10A9FF and #FF73B0, in a matching color. The bottom row has three larger generated images. One is a Van Gogh-style oil painting of Mount Fuji in blues. One is a moody bedroom with blue neon light and warm bedside lamps. One is a woman in a pink checked kimono and an orange hat, among cherry blossoms. Handwritten-style captions sit below, with inline hex codes highlighted as swatches of their own colors. The eye goes first to the glowing, saturated lamps.
caption: One hex-prompt interface for generation and editing. A single finetuned model supports object recoloring and hex-conditioned generation through explicit color values in the prompt.
abstract: Any-color control, specifying an object’s color by any 24-bit hex value instead of a coarse color word, is a practical requirement for image generation and editing in design work. Prior work often relies on dedicated color representations or specialized inference procedures, which can be hard to scale across colors or transfer to new architectures. In this paper, we present Paint-Anything, a single model that reads hex values directly from the prompt for both generation and editing. Our key insight is that the text encoders of recent image generators are language models that already associate hex values with colors, so a generator can learn hex control by grounding these values in object pixels. To this end, we construct Paint-500K, which labels object colors in real images and adds editing pairs, and combine it with pure-color anchors, solid-color images applied only at high-noise timesteps, for lightweight RGB alignment. We further introduce Any Color Benchmark (ACBench), with ACBench-T2I and ACBench-Edit, to measure object-level hex color fidelity. Experiments and ablations show that Paint-Anything substantially improves any-color generation and editing over the base model, suggesting that arbitrary hex-color control can be learned as a native prompt-following behavior of modern image models.
